annotations.title: Animate one image into a clip

description: Animate ONE reference image into ONE AI-generated clip of 4-15 seconds. With no options it is the standard clip: silent, 5 seconds, 480p (for a multi-scene video built from several of the user's pictures, use image_urls on autoshort_generate_chat_video instead). Send the image as image_url (a public https link, JPEG/PNG/WebP, at most 10 MB) or as imageBase64; the stdio package also accepts a local imagePath and uploads it. The image becomes the first frame of the clip. FRAME SHAPE: the clip keeps the image's shape. Without aspect_ratio it is made at the supported ratio nearest to the image (9:16, 1:1, 16:9): a 16:9 image gives a 16:9 clip, a 9:16 image a 9:16 clip. Pass aspect_ratio to choose the ratio yourself. When the ratio differs from the image, the image is scaled to fill the frame and its edges are cut off (centre crop); nothing is padded, blurred or invented, so send the image at the ratio you want to keep all of it. OPTIONS beyond the standard clip (a refusal comes before anything is charged; an account that has never paid makes the standard clip only): duration 4-15 whole seconds on the standard model (default 5). resolution 480p or 720p or 1080p (default 480p; the standard model is 480p only here, a higher resolution needs a model named below). end_image_url / endImageBase64 (stdio: endImagePath): an optional LAST frame the clip ends on, prepared at the same frame shape and screened like the first image. speech { line, language? }: a SPEAKING shot (needs the BUSINESS plan or above). The line (at most 200 characters) is spoken by the character in the image with lip-sync, in a voice the model chooses, and the clip has sound; on the standard model it is always 720p (the only quality with sound). SHOT LIST: pass shots, an ordered list of 2-8 shots { framing, action, speech?, seconds? }, to get several shots with hard cuts inside this ONE clip (one generation, one price) instead of one continuous shot. framing is one of wide, medium, close_up, action, over_shoulder, insert; action says what happens; speech { line, speaker?, language? } makes that shot a spoken line (the clip is then a speaking clip, with its plan and resolution). AutoShort writes the prompt from the list: the length and number of shots, "hard cuts", one numbered sentence per shot, a line that keeps the character identical in every shot, and no subtitles or on-screen text. seconds per shot must add up to duration; leave them out and the clip is spread evenly (each shot at least 1 second); with no duration and every shot's seconds given, the clip is as long as its shots. With shots, motionPrompt is optional (the look, place and mood that hold for every shot) and the price is the same as any clip of that length and resolution. The model decides where the cuts land: the seconds are approximate and a shot can be merged or dropped, so watch the result. Speech is for the stylised or fictional characters this tool accepts; it never makes a real person speak, and a line that names a real person or asks to imitate a real voice is refused. The line is a request to the model: check the words and the lips in the result. MODEL (model: "seedance-2.5"; needs the BUSINESS plan or above): a stronger model that must be asked for by name, never chosen for you. 61 credits per second at 480p and 136 at 720p (about three times the standard model), 4-15 seconds, every clip has sound, and a speaking clip or a shot list with lines may be 480p. A clip that does not fit under today's provider budget is refused before anything is charged (DAILY_CAPACITY). MODEL (model: "wan-3.0"; needs the PRO plan or above, BUSINESS for 1080p): another model that must be asked for by name, never chosen for you. 30 credits per second at 480p, 59 at 720p and 118 at 1080p (the only model with 1080p), 4-15 seconds. A clip without speech is silent; a speaking clip or a shot list with lines has sound at the same price and may be any of the three resolutions (needs the BUSINESS plan or above). It takes a first image, an end image and reference images. A clip that does not fit under today's provider budget is refused before anything is charged (DAILY_CAPACITY; overBudget: true when the clip alone is larger than a whole day's budget, so only a shorter or lower-resolution clip can be made). REFERENCE IMAGES (model "seedance-2.5" or "wan-3.0" only): pass reference_image_urls (1-4 https images of the character) INSTEAD of image_url, with aspect_ratio; the clip then does not start on your image, it keeps the character from the references. Each reference passes the same image check as image_url. PRICE, per second of clip on the standard model: 20 credits at 480p, 89 for a speaking clip; the standard clip is 100 credits (20 x 5 s). These are the standard prices: an account whose credits were bought at full list price pays less, and autoshort_estimate_cost, autoshort_quote_video and autoshort_list_options return the price of the account that asks. ONLY the parameters listed for this tool are accepted: a call that sends any other (an option this server does not offer, or a misspelt name) is refused as a whole before anything is charged, and the answer's nextAction says what to send instead. autoshort_estimate_cost with these same arguments returns the exact price of a call before it is made; the answer returns credits and creditsPerSecond. Charged the moment the job is accepted (not on delivery). The standard clip is open to any plan with enough credits; a never-paid account makes the standard clip only. DRAFT THEN FINAL: make silent takes at 480p, then pass finalize_from (the id of the finished take you keep) together with the SAME image to make it at 720p: same motion prompt, frame shape, length and seed, priced as a 720p clip. Send nothing else with it (no motionPrompt). The final is made on the draft's model, and the standard model is 480p only here: only a draft made with a named model has a final. This is a NEW generation at the higher resolution from the same image, motion prompt, frame shape, length and seed as the draft. Video models do not replay a take exactly: the motion will be close to the draft but not identical. Watch the final before using it. Send the same image again (and the same end image, if the draft had one): the draft's image is deleted when the draft finishes. The answer returns aspectRatio, aspectRatioSource (detected or requested), inputWidth/inputHeight, cropped, durationSeconds, resolution, hasSpeech, hasEndFrame and seed; autoshort_get_video returns aspectRatio and, once COMPLETED, the measured width and height of the clip. ACCEPTED: products, pets, scenery, food, illustrations, and cartoon, anime or other clearly stylised characters (not realistic people, whether real or AI-generated). REJECTED before anything is charged: photos of real people (any realistic human face, to prevent deepfakes), sexual content, anything that may show a child; the answer says why. Only send images the user owns or may use. Rendering is automatic (OpenRouter Seedance): the standard clip is usually ready in about 3 minutes (the answer's typicalSeconds), and a clip is failed and refunded if the video provider has not finished it 8 minutes after the job is sent to it, which is at most about 13 minutes after your call (maxMinutes); a 1080p clip is given proportionally longer, and the answer's maxMinutes is the bound for that clip, so poll autoshort_get_video every 20-30 seconds. Clips submitted together render at the same time (a never-paid account: one at a time); a clip reads PENDING between checks while it renders. If the clip cannot be made (for example the video provider refuses the image on content-policy grounds) the video ends FAILED with the specific reason and the credits are refunded automatically; if it does not come back, check autoshort_get_credit_balance and report a missing refund. The result is labelled AI-generated (aiGenerated: true); keep that label when posting. Retry-safe: the same image, motionPrompt and options return the first job (duplicate: true) for 24 hours instead of charging again, also when a retry adds the aspect_ratio the image already had; a DIFFERENT aspect_ratio is a separate clip, and idempotencyKey forces a separate clip from identical inputs. To turn a TEXT prompt into a moving clip automatically (no photo, no human operator), use autoshort_generate_motion_clip instead.

aspect_ratio.description: Optional frame shape of the clip. Default: the supported ratio nearest to the image's own shape. If it differs from the image, the image is centre-cropped to fill the frame (never padded).

duration.description: Clip length in whole seconds (default 5): up to 15 on the standard model. The price is per second.

endImageBase64.description: Optional LAST frame as a base64-encoded JPG, PNG or WebP file (≤10MB). Alternative to end_image_url.

end_image_url.description: Optional LAST frame: public https link to a JPG, PNG or WebP image (≤10MB). The clip moves from the image to this one. Same content rules as the image.

finalize_from.description: Draft-then-final: the id of one of YOUR finished image-to-video clips. Send it with the SAME image (and end image, if the draft had one), optionally resolution and idempotencyKey, and nothing else. This is a NEW generation at the higher resolution from the same image, motion prompt, frame shape, length and seed as the draft. Video models do not replay a take exactly: the motion will be close to the draft but not identical. Watch the final before using it. Send the same image again (and the same end image, if the draft had one): the draft's image is deleted when the draft finishes.

imageBase64.description: The JPG, PNG or WebP file (≤10MB), base64-encoded. Alternative to image_url.

image_url.description: Public https link to the JPG, PNG or WebP image (≤10MB). Alternative to imageBase64; send one of the two.

model.description: Optional. "standard" (default). "seedance-2.5": about three times the price per second, always with sound, takes reference_image_urls. "wan-3.0": 480p, 720p or 1080p at about half the Seedance 2.5 price per second, silent unless someone speaks, takes reference_image_urls.

motionPrompt.description: Motion, camera and scene direction. Required, except with shots (then optional: the look that holds for every shot) and with finalize_from (the draft's prompt is used).

reference_image_urls.description: model "seedance-2.5" or "wan-3.0" only: 1-4 public https images (JPG, PNG or WebP, ≤10MB each) of the character, sent as references INSTEAD of image_url / imageBase64. Needs aspect_ratio. Same content rules as the image.

resolution.description: Output resolution (default 480p; a speaking clip is always 720p on the standard model; 1080p is model "wan-3.0" only). A higher resolution costs more per second and needs a higher plan.

shots.description: Optional shot list: 2-8 shots with hard cuts inside this one clip, in order. AutoShort writes the prompt from it. Not together with speech (put each line in its shot).

action.description: What happens in the shot, in one sentence (at most 240 characters). Camera angle or movement can be said here ("low angle", "from behind").

seconds.description: Optional length of this shot in seconds (one decimal at most). All shots together must add up to duration.

speech.description: Optional: a line spoken in this shot, with lip-sync. Makes the clip a speaking clip (720p on the standard model).

language.description: Optional language of the line: a code or a name, for example "vi" or "Vietnamese".

speaker.description: Who says it, as the prompt should name them, for example "the swordsman" or "she". Default: the character.

speech.description: Optional: make the character in the image SPEAK one line, with lip-sync and sound. The clip is then 720p on the standard model.

language.description: Optional language of the line: a code or a name, for example "vi" or "Vietnamese".

line.description: The words to speak, exactly (at most 200 characters; one short line fits one clip).
